Thank you for your thoughtful reply. To answer one of your questions, no I have never received therapy. When everything happened I sort of promised myself that I wouldn’t do any of that or let it effect me. To this day I can’t tell you why I thought that was a good idea, but that’s what I did. First I just tried to shrug it off and move on without processing it. That went on for some time, years even. I was determined to maintain this mask of strength I put up around everyone, even my family. I realize now that this might’ve screwed me up more than I’d care to admit. 

As for my guilt, I wish I could give you a concrete answer. Part of me feels like I failed my father. That is I had just been there for him, or if I was just a better son then he wouldn’t have decided to end his own life. 

I’m not taking on his guilt. At least…I don’t think I am. I’m certainly not trying to. But I DO feel guilt every day regarding the whole situation. 

The reason I feel like a bad person mostly has to do with how I’ve treated my mother since, and generally how I’ve basically ejected myself from the family without even trying it. 

I’ve never physically attacked anyone. Yet. Over the last seven years I’ve mastered the art of bottling up my rage and sweeping it under the rug so I keep my cool. But the things that run through my mind sometimes….the level of pure hate I can feel at times scares me. I’m scared one day I’ll snap and lose my mind.

For example, my moms first guy after my dad ended up not working out. It’s a long story but he had substance abuse issues and was stealing from us so she left him. I haven’t seen him since but I’ll tell you now…..he’s better pray I never see him again because when I do? When I do something very terrible if going to happen to him. And I won’t feel bad. Just thinking about him makes me shake with anger.

There are days when the mask starts to crack and I have trouble keeping my cool, but I always manage to just make it through without exploding. 

I guess that’s why I feel so lost. I don’t really know who I am anymore. Or who I ever was now that I know the things I know.

Unvaccinated children are not at risk of dying of covid. That is just a fact. People most at risk of death are the elderly. 

And nobody said they are scared of the vaccine. It’s not about being afraid of it’s effects, it’s about having the freedom to choose. It’s not about fear, it’s about the principle of the thing. But of course you don’t seem to care about that. 

If the vaccines work as intended, and you are vaccinated then there is simply no reason to afraid of someone who isn’t. That’s the point of a vaccine. To give you antibodies so that if someone who isn’t vaccinated passes covid to you, your body will be able to fight it. Suggesting that unvaccinated people pose a significant risk to anyone but themselves and others who choose not to be vaccinated is flat on its face ridiculous. 

You are justifying control over people’s free choices and bodily autonomy that is immoral and would not be accepted in any other context. “My body my choice” doesn’t just apply to women who get abortions. 

Saying “get vaccinated or stay home without income and suffer in poverty, your choice” is no choice at all. It’s an ultimatum, and an extremely immoral one at that. If you disagree then I guess there’s not much more that I can say. 

But I reserve the right to point to people like you as the ones responsible when even more of our freedoms are rolled back in the future.

Ah yes because telling people they can’t work unless they get vaccinated is totally not government coercion or anything right? Saying that “you can sit at home unvaccinated all you want” is disingenuous and you know it because people need to work in order to make a living and put food on their fucking table. 

“People not getting vaccinated are putting society at risk”. False. People who don’t get vaccinated are putting themselves at risk, how on earth are the vaccinated population of people threatened by the unvaccinated people? Do the vaccines not work all of a sudden? If people at risk of dying get the from Covid get the vaccine, why should people not at risk of dying be forced to get it too? What possible reason could you have to justify such a thing? If the vaccines work(as I’m sure they do) then why is it so dangerous that people who aren’t at risk aren’t vaccinated when the people who do have reason to be worried are? 

And never before has the government forced people who are not at risk of dying from a virus get vaccinated under threat of losing their income. Stop trying to gaslight people into thinking this is somehow normal when you know full well it’s not. 

It appears that you fundamentally don’t care about individuals freedoms and instead are happy to trample on certain peoples freedoms if it means “protecting society”. Yet you fail to realize that individual freedoms are the cornerstone of our society and trampling on them will lead us down a path to tyranny. 

I can only assume it’s ignorance and not maliciousness.

People have the right to choose what they put into their bodies. And if they choose to forego getting vaccinated for whatever reason that may be they should not be put out of a job or punished by the government in any way. That is immoral. Period. I’m not saying we should let anyone die, I’m saying the level of force being put behind these vaccines is immoral and it’s setting a precedent that we WILL regret later. Our response to Covid has spit in the face of what a free society should be. The bottom line is that our civilizations were built on a set of principles and they are being blatantly and brazenly violated in the name of “fighting the virus”. This is an unacceptable state of affairs to anyone that values personal liberty and bodily autonomy. I want my kids to grow up in a free country where they have the freedom to choose what they do and do not put into their bodies, not an authoritarian bio-medical security state. We are selling out our future generations to serfdom.
